articles.body: The excitement around 'Ramayana: The Introduction' is set to intensify as the makers prepare to take the much-awaited epic closer to audiences ahead of its theatrical release. According to a report by Mid-Day, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash are expected to lead special fan interactions in Delhi and Bengaluru on October 31 and November 1, respectively. A possible Hyderabad summit is also being planned, as the makers look to build a strong pan-India connect for Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic.Ranbir Kapoor and Yash to lead fan events in Delhi and Bengaluru for 'Ramayana Part 1' promotionsAccording to Mid Day, Ranbir Kapoor, who portrays Lord Ram, is expected to spearhead the Delhi fan meet on October 31. A day later, Yash, who plays Ravana, will reportedly host the Bengaluru leg on November 1. The reported plan is part of the film's wider promotional strategy, with the makers aiming to connect with audiences across different regions before the film arrives in cinemas. An industry source cited by Mid-Day said the intention is to create a pan-India connect, with Ranbir and Yash leading the interactions in their respective cities.A summit in Hyderabad is also reportedly being discussed, potentially around a day before the film's India release. The format is yet to be finalised, but the event could draw more than 4,000 people, according to the report. The makers are also said to be keen on strengthening the film's reach in the South, while its official premiere is expected to take place in Mumbai.'Ramayana Part 1' set for global release on November 6, 2026Positioned as a global Indian production, 'Ramayana' brings together an international team of technicians and is being filmed for IMAX, with DNEG handling its visual effects. The Oscar-winning VFX company, known for its work on films including 'Dune', 'Interstellar' and 'Inception', is associated with the project through producer Namit Malhotra. According to Variety, Sony Pictures Entertainment has now announced that 'Ramayana: Part One' will release worldwide on November 6, 2026, timed around the Diwali festivities, while the second instalment is expected to arrive during Diwali 2027.According to The Hollywood Reporter, Sony has secured the film’s worldwide distribution rights across international markets, while Prime Focus Studios will oversee its release in India. The film is also expected to arrive in several languages, catering to audiences across different global territories.'Ramayana Part 1' synopsis: Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram and Yash as RavanaDirected by Nitesh Tiwari, 'Ramayana Part 1' brings one of India's most revered epics to the big screen on a massive scale. Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Ram, with Sai Pallavi portraying Sita and Yash stepping into the role of Ravana. Sunny Deol plays Lord Hanuman, while Ravie Dubey features as Lakshman. The ensemble also includes Rakul Preet Singh, Lara Dutta and several other prominent actors. The story follows Lord Ram's journey, his relationship with Sita and the conflict that eventually brings him face-to-face with the formidable king of Lanka, Ravana. Conceived as a two-part cinematic epic, the film aims to combine the emotional and spiritual core of the Ramayana with large-scale filmmaking, extensive visual effects and international technical expertise.Sunny Deol's Lord Hanuman appearance reportedly being kept under wrapsOne of the biggest talking points surrounding 'Ramayana Part 1' has been the absence of Sunny Deol's Lord Hanuman from the film's first trailer. According to a recent Bollywood Hungama report, the makers may be deliberately saving Hanuman's major appearance for the climax of the first instalment. The strategy could turn the character's introduction into a significant theatrical moment and potentially leave audiences with a cliffhanger leading into the second part. Sunny Deol's portrayal has already generated curiosity among industry insiders. A select group reportedly saw a brief glimpse of the actor as Hanuman during an exclusive presentation at CinemaCon 2026 in Las Vegas. The report described the actor as being presented in a never-before-seen avatar, while suggesting that keeping his full look away from the public could make the eventual reveal more impactful.15-minute 'Ramayana' footage impresses exhibitors at Big Cine Expo 2026The film also received a fresh boost following an exclusive screening at Big Cine Expo 2026 in Chennai. Approximately 15 minutes of previously unreleased footage was shown to exhibitors during the event held on August 18 and 19. According to Bollywood Hungama, the presentation included visuals and creatures that have not yet been shown publicly, including a one-eyed daitya. Attendees were reportedly prohibited from recording the footage. The visual effects and scale of the project drew strong reactions, with one exhibitor comparing the VFX to the level of a major Hollywood production such as The Lord of the Rings.The preview was particularly significant because it gave cinema exhibitors an early look at the film's visual world beyond the material released in its public promotional campaign. articles.body: The much-awaited ‘Baap’ is set to offer fans a glimpse of its four leading men in a completely different avatar. Sunny Deol, Mithun Chakraborty, Sanjay Dutt and Jackie Shroff have come together for a lively promotional song that combines their trademark action image with dance and camaraderie. Producer Ahmed Khan and director Vivek Chauhan recently filmed the music video, despite the principal photography of the film having been completed in April 2025. The track was shot in June on a specially constructed mill set at Madh Island.The promotional video is expected to feature the four stars together while also incorporating several action moments from the film.Dance, action and plenty of camaraderieThe idea of bringing the veteran actors together for a dance number had been discussed earlier. articles.title: Clint Eastwood, 96 años, sobre la vejez: "Cuando me levanto todos los días, no dejo entrar al viejo"
articles.standfirst: A pesar de rozar la centena, el actor y director se acaba de retirar de la industria cinematográfica
articles.summary: A pesar de rozar la centena, el actor y director se acaba de retirar de la industria cinematográfica
articles.body: Cumplir años y envejecer, en algunas ocasiones, no es lo mismo. Y es que hay quienes creen que lo segundo es una cuestión de actitud. Entre ellos, está Clint Eastwood. A pesar de tener 96 años, el actor y director sigue viviendo con la misma intensidad del primer día, por lo que se acaba de apartar de su trabajo en la industria cinematográfica. Hay que tener en cuenta que Eastwood comenzó su carrera en el año 1959, con la serie ‘Rawhide’. Es decir, ha estado 67 años en activo y no hay ningún atisbo de abandonar su profesión. Pero su actitud no sólo se ve reflejada en su trabajo, también en el día a día, en su relación con los demás. La edad no le limita a la hora de decidir qué hacer, cómo hacerlo o qué sueños aparcar para siempre. El cantante de country Toby Keith le preguntó a Eastwood qué hacía para seguir tan activo a pesar de rozar los 100 años. Su reflexión fue una lección de vida para el artista. El actor y director respondió: “Me levanto todos los días, no dejo entrar al viejo”. Unas palabras que le sirvieron de inspiración para componer la canción de su película ‘Mula’, llamada ‘No dejes entrar al viejo’. “Toda mi vida he intentado levantarme y hacer algo, ser productivo y mantenerme ocupado”, añadió Eastwood en su respuesta. Con 94 años, el director cerró su etapa en el cine con una de sus mejores películas, ‘El Jurado Nº 2’. Lo cierto es que él nunca confirmó que su trabajo en el cine había terminado. No obstante, su hijo Kyle Eastwood lo desveló en su lugar. “Muchos recuerdos entrañables de haber trabajado con él. Ahora está jubilado, tiene 95 años. Pero tuve la gran fortuna de poder trabajar con él en varias películas”, aseguró en una entrevista concedida a France 3.

articles.title: Un reportero de RTVE sufre un cabezazo en la manifestación en Madrid a favor de Ceuta: “No son casos aislados”
articles.standfirst: José Pablo López, presidente del ente público, denuncia el trato a sus trabajadores
articles.summary: José Pablo López, presidente del ente público, denuncia el trato a sus trabajadores
articles.body: La tensión crece en toda España respecto a la crisis en Ceuta, desatada el pasado 31 de julio tras la entrada masiva de miles de personas desde Marruecos. La sociedad está molesta por la forma en que algunos medios de comunicación abordan ciertas informaciones y, en los últimos días, se han vivido escenas problemáticas, como la agresión sufrida por Jesús Poveda, de ‘Malas Lenguas’, en la Plaza de Cibeles. José Pablo López, presidente de Radio Televisión Española (RTVE), ha denunciado los hechos en un comunicado publicado en X, la red social de Elon Musk. En las imágenes, se observa a Poveda en una conexión en directo desde la céntrica plaza de la capital de España y, de repente, uno de los manifestantes a favor de Ceuta y amaga con propinarle un cabezazo. “Hoy le ha tocado a Jesús Poveda en Madrid y a otros compañeros de informativos en Ceuta y Barcelona y a equipos del programa Mañaneros. No son casos aislados. Llevamos más de un mes soportando insultos y agresiones cada vez que salimos a informar”, lamenta el directivo del ente público. Para López, el trato que están recibiendo algunos periodistas por desempeñar su labor en un contexto complejo es injusto: “Aunque algunos creen que es un juego divertido, el señalamiento político y mediático contra los profesionales de RTVE tiene consecuencias en la calle. Agredir a los informadores es dinamitar la democracia”. En las imágenes difundidas, se observa a un hombre increpando al reportero de ‘Malas Lenguas’ y coloca su cabeza sobre la del empleado de RTVE con un leve toque. A pesar de que la mayoría trató de mediar para que el asunto no llegara a mayores, Jesús Poveda anunció en directo que se veía obligado a marcharse: “No nos dejan hacer nuestro trabajo”.

articles.title: Ludlow Food Festival hopes for more visitors amid cost rises
articles.summary: The festival, which includes workshops, takes place from 11 to 13 September and is in its 32nd year.
articles.body:
A food festival cannot continue in its current format if visitor numbers do not improve, said organisers.

Ludlow Food Festival will be held at Ludlow Castle from 11 to 13 September and is in its 32nd year - hosting more than 100 food and drink exhibitors, as well as workshops, musicians and entertainers.

But the Ludlow Marches Food and Drink Board of Directors said that rising costs, economic pressures and technology changes meant holding the event had "never been more difficult".

"Whilst this year's September festival could be the best yet... rising costs mean that this could be the last one in the current format unless we see more people through the castle gates," it said.

The board of directors is a not-for-profit organisation and although some staff are employed, the majority are volunteers.

Its statement added that the festival "weathered the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression and re-emerged after Covid, but now "stands at a cross roads".

During the pandemic, the festival transitioned to an online format and said it needed to raise £40,000 by December 2020 or would be forced to close.

In 2024, the event was rebranded the Ludlow Marches Food and Drink Festival.

"These festivals are about much more than a weekend event," the organisers said.

"They support local producers, attract visitors to the town, generate significant economic benefits for businesses across the region, and help maintain Ludlow's reputation as one of Britain's great food destinations

"If Ludlow Food Festival means something to you, this year is the year to support it."

Several new features have been added in hopes of attracting more visitors.

These includes a food theatre, cookery school, food workshops for children, and a soundtrack stage.

articles.title: Milford Haven boy, 16, who stabbed teacher in head sentenced to four years
articles.summary: Vicki Williams feared she would die in the classroom attack at Milford Haven Comprehensive School.
articles.body:
A pupil who stabbed a teacher in the head with a kitchen knife after asking her to check his homework has been sentenced to four-and-a-half years in youth detention.

The 16-year-old boy followed Vicki Williams into her empty classroom at Milford Haven Comprehensive School, Pembrokeshire, after asking for help with his work on 5 February.

The teenager pulled a knife from his bag and lunged at her, Swansea Crown Court previously heard, with Williams saying she feared she would die .

After the trial in July, he was found not guilty of attempted murder but guilty of wounding with intent.

On Thursday, Judge Thomas told the court there was a "significant degree of planning" and that "time stood still" for Williams.

During the trial, Williams said the attack "came out of nowhere" after the boy - who cannot be named due to a court order - asked her for help with his work at the end of the school day.

He closed the classroom door behind him and Williams noticed him looking through his bag as he asked her if his work "was correct".

She said he suddenly pulled a large kitchen knife from the bag, and stabbed her in her head.

Williams grabbed the knife, pushed the boy back with her legs, and screamed.

She had injuries to her head, back and hands and said the boy looked at her with "pure hatred" .

During the sentencing hearing, the court heard Williams did not know if she would be able to return to work.

She will start therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) this week, and said in her victim personal statement that she felt "sadness, anger and guilt" after the incident.

"Sadness is the most predominant, I focus too much on what could have happened to me," she added.

"I'm in disbelief about what's happened."

She said her daughter had "almost been left without a mum".

"I'm scared because I don't know what I'm going to do going forward," she added.

"My fellow teachers and I don't deserve this because we work so hard.

"I didn't ask for this. Leaving teaching should have been my choice to make."

She said she had returned to the school with a colleague during the summer holidays, and had realised how closely she had been "pinned" to the wall behind her desk.

During the trial, a colleague who rushed to help described Williams's screams as "gut-wrenching".

CCTV footage showed the teenager running away from the school after the attack.

He was later detained at his grandmother's house after telling her that "something went" in his head .

The boy told the jury he had brought the knife to school as a "game" with his friends, which involved bringing "random household objects" to see what they could "get away with".

He said the incident was "an accident" and previously pleaded guilty to possessing a bladed article on school premises.

During the hearing on Thursday, he stood in the dock in a blue shirt, with his family in the public gallery.

Matthew Roberts, defending him, said he was of "clean character" and "well behaved" before the incident.

He told the court his client had made "excellent progress" since being in youth detention.

The boy is due to be released after half of the sentence period, but the court heard his release date could be changed depending on potential amendments to the early release scheme.

Sentencing the boy to four-and-a-half years in a youth detention centre, Judge Thomas said it was "pure luck" Williams had not been seriously injured or worse.

"I don't know why you attacked Mrs Williams with that knife, you never told anybody why you did it," the judge said.

"I think it may have been that in some way she had upset you, but I don't know for certain why.

"What I do know for certain is that you took a knife that day to school because you wanted to really hurt her with it."

He added the boy knew he was "bigger and stronger" than Williams.

"It was pure luck that she didn't have far worse injuries, even fatal injuries," he said.

The judge also referred to another school stabbing in south-west Wales, at Ysgol Dyffryn Aman, where a teenager stabbed two teachers and a pupil in April 2024 .

"The court have to try and keep teachers safe from attacks," he said.

"This is the second case of a school pupil stabbing a teacher in a school in the last couple of years.

"I want anyone who is ever thinking of doing the same to know what will happen to them."

Jonathan Pritchard, of the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said the incident was a "shocking display of violence" towards a "teacher doing their job".

"The teacher showed great courage in what must have been a terrifying incident," he said.

articles.title: R Madhavan killed the audition for 'Swades', what an actor,' recalls writer, reveals the film was originally written for Aamir Khan, finally Shah Rukh Khan stepped in
articles.summary: Ashutosh Gowariker’s Swades is now remembered as one of Shah Rukh Khan’s most acclaimed performances, but the film’s journey to the screen looked very.
articles.body: Ashutosh Gowariker’s Swades is now remembered as one of Shah Rukh Khan’s most acclaimed performances, but the film’s journey to the screen looked very different in its early stages. Before Khan became Mohan Bhargava, the role was originally written with Aamir Khan in mind, when the project was still titled Desh.Actor and writer Amin Hajee, who played Bagha in Lagaan and later became part of the writing team on Swades, recently revisited the film’s unusual casting history in a conversation with Siddharth Kannan.According to Hajee, Swades was conceived as Ashutosh Gowariker’s immediate follow-up to Lagaan, with Aamir once again set to headline the project. Aamir was also attached to the film as a producer through Aamir Khan Productions.“At that time Aamir was supposed to play Shah Rukh Khan’s role. It was originally Aamir, always, from the start. After Lagaan, the next film was this with Aamir,” Hajee recalled.The problem, however, was not with the basic premise. Aamir reportedly liked the story but had reservations about the screenplay and wanted to spend time developing certain elements further.“Aamir did not like some things that we had done. That version of the script he did not like. He liked the plot,” Hajee said.There was another major complication: Aamir simply did not have the time to work on the script to the extent Gowariker wanted. Known for concentrating on one film at a time, he was unable to commit to the lengthy development process while Gowariker was keen to begin his next project after Lagaan.“Aamir loved the plot. He was just wanting to work on things. But the more important thing is that he didn’t have the time. Aamir does one film at one time.”Aamir eventually decided not to act in the film, although he was initially prepared to remain involved as its producer. He gave Gowariker the freedom to cast another actor.“Aamir was very kind. Aamir said, ‘Okay, I will still produce it. You decide who you want to play that role.’”Hajee stressed that Aamir’s eventual departure as producer was a separate development and was not simply a consequence of Shah Rukh replacing him as the lead. Rather, Aamir understood that Gowariker was ready to move forward and should not have to wait for his availability.“It is not that Shah Rukh entered and Aamir exited as producer also,” Hajee clarified. “Aamir exited because Aamir understood that right now Ashutosh is raring to make his next film.”With the lead role now open, Gowariker began looking at other possibilities. Hrithik Roshan was among the actors who heard the narration, while R Madhavan also auditioned. Hajee remains particularly impressed by Madhavan’s performance during the audition.“We narrated the script to Hrithik Roshan also. Madhavan also gave the audition — and what an audition. He killed it. He is a great actor.”Then came Shah Rukh Khan.Hajee recalled that Shah Rukh was interested in watching Lagaan, which had become a major success. A special screening was arranged for the actor at Adlabs in Film City, and Hajee happened to sit beside him during the screening.The film evidently made a strong impression on Shah Rukh. By the end of it, he had decided that he wanted to work with Gowariker and take on the role that had originally been intended for Aamir.“He said, ‘I should be in Ashu’s next film. My father was a freedom fighter. I should do Desh. I should be Mohan Bhargava.’”Shah Rukh then contacted Gowariker directly and made his interest clear.“He called Ashu and said, ‘Ashu, I have to be in your next film. You are a great director. I want to be a part of your next film.’”The two already had a professional connection, having worked together previously, including on the television series Circus. After Shah Rukh came on board, he was tested for the role, and the rest became a matter of cinematic fate.“Then we tested, and I think it’s all destiny. So Shah Rukh did Swades and I became a writer, and Charlotte co-wrote it with us,” Hajee said.Hajee also remembered an intriguing comment Shah Rukh made about stepping into projects that had previously been associated with Aamir. According to the writer, Shah Rukh said he trusted Aamir’s involvement enough to take on such a film without even reading the script.“The film that Aamir couldn’t do, I did without reading the script because I knew that must be great.”He then connected the thought to another famous example from Shah Rukh’s career:“Look at the history — Darr, Aamir didn’t do, Shah Rukh did.”Released in December 2004, Swades did not make a major impact at the box office during its initial theatrical run. Its standing, however, changed considerably with time. The film gradually developed a devoted following, and Shah Rukh’s understated portrayal of NASA scientist Mohan Bhargava came to be regarded as one of the most nuanced performances of his career.What began as a project built around Aamir Khan ultimately found its defining face in Shah Rukh Khan — turning Swades into a striking example of how a film’s casting journey can completely reshape its legacy.Give your child the gift of confidence!
